open_decision: The laws do not fix the order in which the added starter rows are appended to the registry.
input: config: enable = false, no adapter locked; starter = [{id 2, adapter 1, model 2, enabled true}, {id 4, adapter 2, model 5, enabled true}]; registry = [] (empty).
result_a: designA appends in starter order: [{id 2, adapter 1, model 2, enabled false}, {id 4, adapter 2, model 5, enabled false}].
result_b: designB appends in reverse starter order: [{id 4, adapter 2, model 5, enabled false}, {id 2, adapter 1, model 2, enabled false}].
reason: Both designs append only absent starters, disable them by default, leave no starter id missing, and add nothing on a second run, so each passes all seven laws. The laws never state the order of the added rows, so the two registries differ.
